entries.18.12: '"That which is joined with unrighteousness is not to be praised, nor that which is turned against the world. Having done a deed of wickedness, you boast of conquering your brother.
entries.18.13: '"Where were you before, that you practised dharma alone and won a boon? I have never before heard such words as you speak of yourself.
entries.18.14: '"Stand now; you shall not go from me alive, evil-minded one. Today I shall send you with sharp arrows to the house of Yama."
entries.18.15: 'Then the king took up his bow and arrows and went out in wrath to the fight; but Samvarta barred his way.
entries.18.16: 'That great sage said to Marutta with affection, "If my word is to be heard, this fight is not fitting for you.
entries.18.17: '"This rite of Maheshvara, if left unfinished, would burn up your line.
entries.18.18: '"How can there be battle for one under consecration? How can there be anger in one consecrated? And victory is always in doubt, and this rakshasa is very hard to conquer."
entries.18.19: 'At his teacher's word Marutta, lord of the earth, turned back; and laying aside his bow and arrows he composed himself and turned his face to the sacrifice.
entries.18.20: 'Then Shuka, taking him for conquered, proclaimed aloud, "Ravana is victorious!" and let loose a shout of joy.
entries.18.21: 'And having devoured the great sages who were there, come to the sacrifice, and being sated with their blood, Ravana went again over the earth.
entries.18.22: 'When Ravana had gone, the gods with Indra, the dwellers in heaven, came back each to his own form and spoke to those creatures.
entries.18.23: 'Indra in his gladness said then to the peacock with its dark plumage, "I am pleased with you, knower of dharma; you shall have no fear from serpents.
entries.18.24: '"And this thousand of eyes shall be upon your tail; and when I send down rain you shall feel a joy that is the mark of my favour." Thus Indra, lord of the gods, gave the peacock a boon.
entries.18.25: 'For before that, king, the plumes of peacocks were dark; and having won that boon from the lord of the gods, all peacocks came to be as they are.
entries.18.26: 'The king of dharma said, Rama, to the crow that sat in the hall, "Bird, I am well pleased with you; hear the word of one who is pleased.
entries.18.27: '"As other creatures are afflicted by me with diseases of many kinds, those shall have no power over you, since I am pleased — of that there is no doubt.
entries.18.28: '"You have no fear of death by my boon, bird; you shall live so long as men do not kill you.
entries.18.29: '"And those men in my realm who are afflicted by the fear of hunger — when you have eaten, they with their kinsmen shall be satisfied."
entries.18.30: 'And Varuna said to the swan that sported in the waters of Ganga: "Hear a word of favour, lord of the winged.
entries.18.31: '"A colour lovely and gentle, like the disc of the moon, shall be yours, radiant as pure foam.
entries.18.32: '"Coming into contact with my body you shall be beautiful for ever, and you shall have a joy beyond compare. This is the mark of my favour."
entries.18.33: 'For before that, Rama, the colour of swans was dark and pale together — their wings edged with dark and their breasts spotless as the tips of young grass.
entries.18.34: 'Then Vaishravana said to the lizard that sat upon the rock, "I give you the colour of gold, for I too am pleased with you.
entries.18.35: '"And your head shall always be of that substance and shall never fade. This colour of gold shall be yours by my favour."
entries.18.36: 'Having thus given boons to them at that festival of sacrifice, the gods turned back with the king and went again to their own dwellings.'
entries.19.1: 'Then, having conquered Marutta, the lord of rakshasas went on; and Dashanana, seeking battle, came to the cities of kings.
entries.19.2: 'Coming to those lords of kings, who were like Mahendra and Varuna, the lord of rakshasas said, "Let battle be given me,
entries.19.3: '"or else say, 'We are conquered.' This is my fixed resolve. For those who do otherwise there is no deliverance."
entries.19.4: 'Then those kings, fearless and wise and settled in dharma, mighty though they were, took counsel with one another and said, "We are conquered," knowing the strength of their enemy's boon.
entries.19.5: 'Dushyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, King Gaya and Pururavas — all these kings said, dear one, "We are conquered."
entries.19.6: 'Then Ravana, lord of rakshasas, came to Ayodhya,
entries.19.7: 'well guarded by Anaranya as Amaravati is guarded by Shakra. To that tiger among men, the equal of Purandara in strength,
entries.19.8: 'Ravana came and said to the king, "Give me battle, or else say, 'I am conquered.' This is my command."
entries.19.9: 'The lord of Ayodhya, hearing the words of that evil-souled one, Anaranya in great wrath answered the lord of rakshasas:
entries.19.10: '"Single combat is given you by me, lord of rakshasas. Stand ready at once, and I shall be ready too."
entries.19.11: 'Then, having heard beforehand what had passed, that great army of the king — that host bent upon the rakshasa's destruction — marched out.
entries.19.12: 'Ten thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses, many thousands of chariots and of footmen, best of men,
entries.19.13: 'covering the earth, marched out with foot and chariot to the battle. Then there arose a great fight, skilled one in war,
entries.19.14: 'a wonderful fight between King Anaranya and the lord of rakshasas. But coming against that army of Ravana, the host of that lord of earth
entries.19.15: 'perished utterly, like an oblation poured into the fire. Having fought a long while and shown the highest valour,
entries.19.16: 'coming against him who blazed, they were quickly reduced to a remnant; they entered the press there like moths into a flame, and that army perished like an oblation poured into fire.
entries.19.17: 'And that king saw his great army perishing, as a hundred forest streams perish when they come to the great ocean.
entries.19.18: 'Then, twanging with his own hand a bow like the bow of Shakra, the king in a swoon of anger came against Ravana.
entries.19.19: 'By Anaranya those counsellors of his — Maricha, Shuka and Sarana, together with Prahasta — were broken and fled like deer.
entries.19.20: 'Then that delight of the Ikshvaku line brought down eight hundred arrows upon the head of that king of the rakshasas.
entries.19.21: 'But those arrows falling upon him did him no hurt anywhere, like showers of water falling from the clouds upon a mountain's crest.
entries.19.22: 'Then the king of rakshasas in anger struck the king upon the head with the flat of his hand, and he fell from his chariot.
entries.19.23: 'That king fell to the ground, his limbs shaking and trembling, like a sala tree burnt by lightning and fallen in the forest.
entries.19.24: 'And the rakshasa said to that Ikshvaku lord of earth with a laugh, "What fruit have you gained now by fighting against me?
entries.19.25: '"There is none in the three worlds who could give me single combat, king of men. I think that, being sunk in pleasures, you have not heard of my strength."
entries.19.26: 'As he spoke thus, the king, his life ebbing, said: "What can be done here? Time cannot be overstepped.
entries.19.27: '"I am not conquered by you, rakshasa, for all your praising of yourself. I have fallen by time alone; you have only been its instrument.
entries.19.28: '"But what can I do now, when my life is spent? For I was not slain by you with my face turned away in the fight, rakshasa.
entries.19.29: '"Because you have insulted the Ikshvakus, I shall speak a word. If I have given, if I have offered, if I have done good penance, if I have guarded my subjects rightly, then let my word be true:
entries.19.30: '"There shall be born in this line of the great-souled Ikshvakus one named Rama, the son of Dasharatha, who shall take your life."
entries.19.31: 'Then the drum of the gods was beaten, deep as a thundercloud; and as that curse was uttered a rain of flowers fell from the sky.
entries.19.32: 'Then that king, lord of kings, went to the station of the third heaven; and when that king had gone to heaven, the rakshasa went his way.'
entries.20.1: 'Then the lord of rakshasas, terrifying mortals upon the earth, came upon Narada, that bull among sages, in a dense cloud.
entries.20.2: 'The night-ranger Dashagriva saluted him and, having asked after his welfare, asked also the reason of his coming.
entries.20.3: 'And Narada, the divine sage of great splendour and measureless light, seated upon the back of a cloud, said to Ravana who stood in the Pushpaka:
entries.20.4: '"Stay, gentle lord of rakshasas, son of Vishrava. I am pleased with your high birth and with your mighty deeds of valour.
entries.20.5: '"By your slaying of the daityas as Vishnu did, and by your harrying of gandharvas and serpents, and by your combats, I am greatly satisfied.
entries.20.6: '"I shall say something to you, if you will hear what should be heard. And having heard it, best of rakshasas, act afterwards. Give me your attention, dear one, while I speak.
entries.20.7: '"Why is this world being slain by you, dear one, who cannot be slain by the gods? This world is already slain, since it has come under the sway of death.
entries.20.8: '"You who cannot be slain by gods or danavas or daityas, by yakshas, gandharvas or rakshasas — it is not fitting that you should afflict the world of men.
entries.20.9: '"Who would strike such a world as this, always confused about its own good, hedged about with great calamities, joined with a hundred kinds of age and disease?
entries.20.10: '"With such unwished-for things coming ceaselessly, wherever it may be — what man of understanding would seek to make war upon the world of men?
entries.20.11: '"Do not destroy this world, which wastes away, struck down by fate, worn by hunger and thirst and age, bewildered by despair and grief.
entries.20.12: '"Look, mighty-armed lord of rakshasas, upon the world of men — so deluded, so strange in its purposes, whose course cannot be known.
entries.20.13: '"Here music and dancing are enjoyed by glad people, and there others in their affliction weep with streaming eyes and faces.
entries.20.14: '"Deluded by love of mother and father and children, by the sweetness of wives and kinsmen, these people are destroyed and do not perceive their own suffering.
entries.20.15: '"Enough of tormenting this world, which is undone by delusion. The world of mortals is already conquered by you, gentle one, and of that there is no doubt.
entries.20.16: '"All of them must go of necessity to Yama's abode. Restrain Yama, then, son of Pulastya, conqueror of your enemies' cities.
entries.20.17: '"When he is conquered, all is conquered, and of that there is no doubt." Being addressed thus, the lord of Lanka, blazing with his own splendour, saluted Narada and said to him, laughing:
entries.20.18: '"Great sage, who take your pleasure among gods and gandharvas and love the fray — I am setting out for the nether world to conquer it.
entries.20.19: '"Then, having conquered the three worlds and brought the nagas and the gods beneath my sway, I shall churn the ocean, that dwelling of waters, for the nectar."
entries.20.20: 'Then the venerable sage Narada said to Dashagriva: "Where are you going now by this other road?
entries.20.21: '"This road that leads toward the city of the king of the dead is very hard to travel; it goes to Yama, and it is not to be assailed, wearer-down of foes."
entries.20.22: 'Then Dashanana let loose a laugh like an autumn cloud and said, "It is done," and spoke these words:
entries.20.23: '"Therefore, brahmin, being set upon slaying the son of Vivasvat, I go to the southern quarter, where the son of the sun is king.
entries.20.24: '"For in my anger, lord, seeking battle, I have vowed that I shall conquer the four guardians of the world.
entries.20.25: '"So I am setting out for the city of the king of the dead, and I shall join with death itself him who brings affliction upon living creatures."
entries.20.26: 'Having spoken thus and saluted the sage, Dashagriva went with his ministers and entered the southern quarter.
entries.20.27: 'And Narada of great splendour stood a moment in meditation, and that best of brahmins pondered, like a fire without smoke:
entries.20.28: '"He by whom the three worlds with Indra are afflicted, with all that moves and does not move — when a life is spent, its time comes by law; how then shall that Time be conquered?
entries.20.29: '"He who is the witness of what each has given and done, like a second fire — the worlds, when they come to their senses, will be conquered by that great one.
entries.20.30: '"He before whom the three worlds flee always in terror — how shall this lord of rakshasas go against him of his own accord?
entries.20.31: '"He who is the ordainer and the disposer of what is well done and ill done, by whom the three worlds are conquered — how shall he be conquered?
entries.20.32: '"Or what other course will he devise and follow? Curiosity has come upon me; I shall go to Yama's abode
entries.20.33: '"to see for myself the encounter between these two, Yama and the rakshasa."'
entries.21.1: 'Having thought thus, that best of brahmins went with swift steps toward Yama's abode, to tell what had happened.
entries.21.2: 'There he saw the god Yama, with Agni before him, setting in order for each living creature what was its due.
entries.21.3: 'And Yama, seeing the great sage Narada arrived there, offered him the guest-water according to dharma and said to him as he sat at ease:
entries.21.4: '"Is all well, divine sage? Does dharma not perish? What is the business of your coming, you who are attended by gods and gandharvas?"
entries.21.5: 'Then the venerable sage Narada said these words: "Let it be heard; I shall tell you, and let provision be made.
entries.21.6: '"This night-ranger named Dashagriva, king of the fathers, is coming to bring you under his sway by his valour, hard though you are to conquer.
entries.21.7: '"It is for this cause that I have come in haste, lord. What now will befall you, whose weapon is the rod?"
entries.21.8: 'At that moment they saw from afar the blazing chariot of that rakshasa coming on like the risen sun.
entries.21.9: 'That mighty one drew near, making that whole region free of darkness with the radiance of the Pushpaka.
entries.21.10: 'And that mighty-armed Dashagriva saw on every side living creatures reaping the fruit of their good deeds and of their evil.
entries.21.11: 'He saw his own soldiers with Yama's followers — with Yama's men, fierce and dreadful of form and terrible.
entries.21.12: 'He saw embodied beings being punished and tormented, crying out with a great cry and giving themselves to bitter wailing,
entries.21.13: 'and being devoured by worms and by dreadful dogs,
entries.21.14: 'and uttering words that pained the ear and struck terror; and many being made to cross the Vaitarani whose waters are blood;
entries.21.15: 'and being scorched again and again upon burning sands; and the unrighteous being cut apart in the wood of sword-leaves,
entries.21.16: 'in Raurava and in the river of caustic and among the razor-edges; and others begging for water, thirsty and hungry,
entries.21.17: 'corpse-like, wasted and wretched, pale, their hair loose, covered with filth and mire, miserable and gaunt, running here and there.
entries.21.18: 'Such Ravana saw upon that road by hundreds and by thousands. And others he saw in fine houses, delighting in the sound of song and music, rejoicing by their own good deeds —
entries.21.19: 'the givers of cows enjoying the milk of cows, the givers of food enjoying food, and the givers of houses their houses, each eating the fruit of his own act,
entries.21.20: 'adorned with gold and jewels and pearls, and with fair women beside them.
entries.21.21: 'Others there, righteous and blazing with their own splendour, the mighty-armed Ravana lord of rakshasas saw.
entries.21.22: 'Then that mighty one, by his valour and by force, set free those who were being torn for their own evil deeds.
entries.21.23: 'Those beings, set free by the rakshasa Dashagriva, had a moment of happiness beyond hope or thought.
entries.21.24: 'As the departed were being released by that mighty rakshasa, their keepers in great wrath rushed upon the lord of rakshasas.
entries.21.25: 'Then a tumult arose from every quarter, of the warriors of the king of dharma, brave men rushing forward.
entries.21.26: 'With darts and iron bars, with pikes and pestles, with spears and javelins, those brave ones by hundreds of thousands rained upon the Pushpaka.
entries.21.27: 'Its seats, its terraces, its platforms and its archways they swiftly broke, like bees upon a flower.
entries.21.28: 'But that chariot Pushpaka, the seat of the gods, though so broken in that fight, remained as it was, imperishable by the power of Brahma.
entries.21.29: 'Countless and vast was the army of that great one, with hundreds and thousands of brave men at its head.
entries.21.30: 'Then with trees and rocks and with hundreds of terraces those ministers of his fought as they wished and as they were able, those great heroes, and King Dashanana with them.
entries.21.31: 'Their limbs smeared with blood and struck by every kind of weapon, the ministers of the lord of rakshasas made a great slaughter.
entries.21.32: 'Those greatly blessed ones struck one another hard with their weapons — the counsellors of Yama and of Ravana, mighty-armed one.
entries.21.33: 'Then Yama's warriors, of great strength, left those ministers and rushed upon Dashanana himself with showers of pikes.
entries.21.34: 'Then, his limbs smeared with blood and his body broken by their blows, the lord of rakshasas shone in the Pushpaka like an ashoka tree in flower.
entries.21.35: 'And he loosed pikes and maces and nooses, spears and javelins and arrows, pestles, rocks and trees, by the strength of his weapon-craft.
entries.21.36: 'And that most dreadful rain of trees and rocks and weapons fell upon Yama's hosts and upon the earth.
entries.21.37: 'But they broke through all of it and turned that weapon aside, and by hundreds of thousands they struck at that dreadful rakshasa who stood alone.
entries.21.38: 'Surrounding him all together, like clouds about a mountain, they beat him with bhindipalas and pikes until he could scarcely breathe.
entries.21.39: 'His armour cast off, wrathful and drenched with streams of blood, he then left the Pushpaka and stood upon the earth.
entries.21.40: 'Then he took his bow and turned again to the battle; and in a moment, coming to his senses, he stood in his wrath like Antaka himself.
entries.21.41: 'Then, fitting to his bow the divine Pashupata weapon, and saying to them, "Stand, stand!", he drew that bow.
entries.21.42: 'Drawing it to his ear, that enemy of Indra loosed the arrow in his wrath, as Shankara loosed his against the three cities.
entries.21.43: 'The form of that arrow was a circle of smokeless flame, like a forest fire raging in the hot season and about to burn a wood.
entries.21.44: 'Wreathed in flame, that arrow, followed by the flesh-eaters, once loosed rushed on, turning thickets and trees to ashes.
entries.21.45: 'The armies of the son of Vivasvat, burnt by its splendour, fell in that battle like trees burnt by a forest fire.
entries.21.46: 'Then that rakshasa of terrible valour, together with his ministers, let loose a mighty roar as though shaking the earth.'
entries.22.1: 'Hearing that great roar of his, the lord son of Vivasvat took his enemy for victorious and knew that his own force was destroyed.
entries.22.2: 'Knowing his warriors slain, his eyes red with anger, he said quickly to his charioteer, "Let my chariot be brought."
entries.22.3: 'His charioteer then brought up that divine great chariot and stood by; and that one of great splendour mounted it. And Mrityu, with dart and mallet in hand, stood before him.
entries.22.4: 'And Kaladanda, the staff of Time by which all this imperishable threefold world is gathered up, stood at his side and took on form — Yama's divine weapon, blazing with splendour like fire.
entries.22.5: 'At his sides were set the nooses of Time, from which there is no escape.
entries.22.6: 'And the mallet stood there embodied, its touch like fire itself.
entries.22.7: 'Then the three worlds were shaken and the dwellers in heaven trembled, seeing Kala thus in wrath, a terror to all the worlds.
entries.22.8: 'Then the charioteer urged on those horses of shining splendour and went with a dreadful roar to where the lord of rakshasas stood.
entries.22.9: 'In a moment those horses, like the horses of Hari and swift as thought, brought Yama to where that battle was joined.
entries.22.10: 'Seeing that chariot so terrible, and Death himself upon it, the counsellors of the lord of rakshasas fled away at once.
entries.22.11: 'Being of light courage, they lost their senses and were tormented by fear, and saying, "We are not able to fight here," they went to the four quarters.
entries.22.12: 'But Dashagriva, seeing that chariot which was a terror to the worlds, was not shaken, nor did fear enter him.
entries.22.13: 'Then Yama came against Ravana and loosed spears and javelins, and in his wrath he cut into Ravana's vital parts.
entries.22.14: 'But Ravana, unmoved, let fly a rain of arrows upon the chariot of Vivasvat's son, as a cloud lets fall its rain.
entries.22.15: 'Then, as great spears and arrows fell upon his broad chest, that rakshasa, tormented by the shafts, could not strike back.
entries.22.16: 'Thus for seven nights was that enemy made senseless and turned away in battle by Yama, the wearer-down of foes, with weapons of many kinds.
entries.22.17: 'And there was a tumultuous fight between those two, Yama and the rakshasa, hero — both desiring victory and neither turning from the field.
entries.22.18: 'Then the gods with the gandharvas, and the siddhas and the great sages, came together to that field of battle, putting Prajapati at their head.
entries.22.19: 'It was as though the worlds were at their dissolution, so wroth were those two — the chief of rakshasas and the lord of the departed.
entries.22.20: 'The lord of rakshasas too, drawing his bow that shone like Indra's thunderbolt, loosed arrows until the sky was left with no space between them.
entries.22.21: 'He struck Mrityu with four shafts and the charioteer with seven, and swiftly struck Yama in his vital parts with a hundred thousand.
entries.22.22: 'Then from the mouth of the angry Yama there came forth the fire of his wrath, wreathed in flame, with his breath and with smoke.
entries.22.23: 'Seeing that marvel there in the presence of gods and danavas, Mrityu and Kala were filled with delight and with fury.
entries.22.24: 'Then Mrityu, angrier still, said to the son of Vivasvat: "Loose me in the fight, that I may slay this sinful rakshasa. This rakshasa shall not stand today; that is the law by its own nature.
entries.22.25: '"Hiranyakashipu the glorious, and Namuchi and Shambara, Visandhi and Dhumaketu, and Bali the son of Virochana,
entries.22.26: '"Shambhu the great king of the daityas, and Vritra and Bana too; royal sages learned in the scriptures, gandharvas and great serpents,
entries.22.27: '"sages and serpents and daityas, yakshas and the hosts of apsaras; and at the turning of an age the earth with its great oceans,
entries.22.28: '"with its mountains, rivers and trees, was brought to destruction, great king. These and many others, mighty and hard to assail,
entries.22.29: '"I have seen laid low; what then is this night-ranger?
entries.22.30: '"Loose me, then, knower of dharma, that I may slay him. For none whom I have looked upon lives, however strong he be.
entries.22.31: '"This is not my own strength; it is the law by its own nature. He whom I have looked upon does not live even a moment longer."
entries.22.32: 'Hearing those words of his, the mighty king of dharma said to Mrityu there, "Stand you back; I shall slay him myself."
entries.22.33: 'Then the lord son of Vivasvat, his eyes red with wrath, hefted in his hand the unfailing staff of Time,
entries.22.34: 'at whose sides all the nooses of Time are set, and beside which the mallet stood embodied, like fire and the thunderbolt.
entries.22.35: 'By the mere sight of it the lives of living creatures are drawn away — how much more of one it touches, or upon whom it falls?
entries.22.36: 'Wreathed in flame, as though burning up the rakshasa, that great weapon quivered at the touch of that mighty one.
entries.22.37: 'Then all fled from that field in terror, and all the gods were troubled, seeing Yama with his staff upraised.
entries.22.38: 'But as Yama was about to strike Ravana with the staff, the Grandsire showed himself to Yama and said:
entries.22.39: '"Mighty-armed son of Vivasvat, of measureless valour — this night-ranger must not be slain by you with that staff.
entries.22.40: '"A boon was given to him by me, bull among the gods. You must not make false the word that I have spoken.
entries.22.41: '"Whoever makes me false, whether god or man, by him the three worlds are made false — of that there is no doubt.
entries.22.42: '"This staff, once loosed in anger, makes no difference between the dear and the hateful; dreadful, a terror to the three worlds, it gathers up all creatures.
entries.22.43: '"It is unfailing against all living beings, one of measureless splendour; the staff of Time was created by me of old, with Death set before it.
entries.22.44: '"So it must not fall upon Ravana's head, gentle one. For if it falls, no creature lives even a moment.
entries.22.45: '"If, when it falls, this rakshasa does not die, or if Dashagriva dies — then either way there is falsehood.
entries.22.46: '"Hold back therefore this staff you have raised against the lord of Lanka. Make me true today, if you have any regard for the worlds."
entries.22.47: 'Being addressed thus, that soul of dharma, Yama, answered: "This staff is turned aside, for you are our master.
entries.22.48: '"But what then can I do, being come to battle? If he cannot be slain by me, protected as he is by a boon —
entries.22.49: '"then I shall vanish from the sight of this rakshasa." And having spoken thus, he disappeared upon the spot with his chariot and his horses.
entries.22.50: 'And Dashagriva, having conquered him and proclaimed his own name, mounted the Pushpaka again and went out from Yama's abode.
entries.22.51: 'And the son of Vivasvat went gladly to the third heaven with the gods and with Brahma at their head, and the great sage Narada with them.'
entries.23.1: 'Then Dashagriva, having conquered Yama, that bull among the gods, Ravana who gloried in battle looked upon his companions.
entries.23.2: 'Seeing Ravana with his limbs drenched in blood and his body broken by blows, the rakshasas came to him rejoicing.
entries.23.3: 'Maricha and the rest, having hailed him for his victory, all boarded the Pushpaka, comforted by Ravana.
entries.23.4: 'Then, going down to the nether world, he entered the treasury of the waters, thronged with hosts of daityas and serpents and well guarded by Varuna.
entries.23.5: 'And going to the city Bhogavati, ruled by Vasuki, he brought the nagas under his sway and went gladly to the city of jewels.
entries.23.6: 'There dwelt the daityas called Nivatakavachas, who had won a boon; and coming upon them, that rakshasa called them out to battle.
entries.23.7: 'And all those sons of Diti, valiant and mighty, took up their many weapons there and rejoiced, wild for the fight.
entries.23.8: 'With pikes and tridents, with thunderbolts, with battle-axes and swords and hatchets, the rakshasas and the danavas in their fury tore at one another.
entries.23.9: 'And as they fought a full year and more went by, and neither side had victory or destruction.
entries.23.10: 'Then the Grandsire, the imperishable refuge of the three worlds, came there swiftly, seated in his finest chariot.
entries.23.11: 'Restraining the Nivatakavachas from that work of war, the aged Grandsire spoke, knowing how the matter stood:
entries.23.12: '"This Ravana cannot be conquered in battle by gods or asuras; nor can you be brought to destruction, even by the gods and danavas together.
entries.23.13: '"Friendship with the rakshasa, therefore, is what I would counsel for you. Among friends nothing is held apart — of that there is no doubt."
entries.23.14: 'Then Ravana made friendship with the Nivatakavachas there, with fire as witness, and was filled with affection for them.
entries.23.15: 'He dwelt with them a year in due form, and Dashanana found there a delight no less than in his own city.
entries.23.16: 'Then, having learned from them a hundred kinds of illusion, he ranged the nether world seeking the city of the lord of waters.
entries.23.17: 'Then, going to the city named Ashmanagara, held by the Kalakeyas, and slaying those Kalakeyas swollen with strength,
entries.23.18: 'he cut down with his sword the husband of Shurpanakha — his own brother-in-law, the mighty Vidyujjihva of great strength, that rakshasa who in the battle was licking with his tongue.
entries.23.19: 'Having conquered him in a moment, he slew four hundred of the daityas.
entries.23.20: 'Then the lord of rakshasas saw the divine dwelling of Varuna, white as a pale cloud and shining like Kailasa.
entries.23.21: 'And there he saw standing the cow Surabhi, pouring out her milk — she from whose flowing milk comes the ocean called the Sea of Milk.
entries.23.22: 'Ravana saw there that source of the best of bulls and cattle, from whom comes the moon, the cool-rayed maker of night;
entries.23.23: 'upon whom the great sages who drink the foam depend for their life; from whom came the nectar of the gods, and the svadha of those who feed upon it —
entries.23.24: 'she whom men in the world call by the name Surabhi. Ravana went round that most wondrous one from left to right,
entries.23.25: 'and entered that dreadful place guarded by forces of many kinds. Then he saw the fine house of Varuna, strewn with a hundred streams, white as an autumn cloud, and ever joyful.
entries.23.26: 'Then, having slain the captains of the guard in battle and been struck by them, he said to the warriors, "Announce this quickly to the king:
entries.23.27: '"'Ravana has come seeking battle; let battle be given him. Or else say with joined palms, "I am conquered," and you shall have no fear.'"
entries.23.28: 'At that moment the sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuna came out in wrath — Go and Pushkara among them.
entries.23.29: 'Those who were endowed with valour and virtue, surrounded by their own forces, yoked their chariots that go where they are wished, blazing with the splendour of the rising sun.
entries.23.30: 'Then there was a fight terrible and making the hair stand on end, between the sons of the lord of waters and the wise Ravana.
entries.23.31: 'And by the ministers of the rakshasa Dashagriva, of great valour, that whole army of Varuna was struck down in a moment.
entries.23.32: 'Seeing their own force in that battle tormented by the net of arrows, Varuna's sons turned back from the work of war.
entries.23.33: 'Standing upon the ground and seeing Ravana in the Pushpaka, they entered the sky at once in their swift-moving chariots.
entries.23.34: 'Then, having gained a station equal to his, there was a great tumultuous battle in the sky between them, like a battle of gods and danavas.
entries.23.35: 'Then with arrows like fire they turned Ravana back in that fight, and in their gladness they let loose cries of many kinds.
entries.23.36: 'Then Mahodara in his fury, seeing his king so treated, cast away the fear of death and looked about him, that hero, longing for the fight.
entries.23.37: 'And those dreadful chariots of theirs, going where they were wished and swift as the wind, were struck by Mahodara with his mace and went down to the earth.
entries.23.38: 'Having slain the warriors and hundreds of the horses of Varuna's sons, he let loose a great roar, seeing them left without chariots.
entries.23.39: 'Their chariots with their horses and their charioteers slain, struck down by Mahodara, fell upon the ground.
entries.23.40: 'But the sons of the great-souled Varuna abandoned their chariots and stood in the sky, those brave ones, and by their own power were not dismayed.
entries.23.41: 'Making their bows ready and piercing Mahodara through, they rushed together in their wrath upon Ravana in the fight.
entries.23.42: 'With arrows loosed from their bows, terrible as thunderbolts, they tore at him in their fury as clouds tear at a great mountain.
entries.23.43: 'Then Dashagriva in anger, breaking forth like the fire of Time, struck them in their vital parts with most dreadful showers of arrows.
entries.23.44: 'And at that the foot-soldiers sank down at once. Then pestles of many kinds, and hundreds of javelins,
entries.23.45: 'and pikes and spears, shataghnis and lances, that unassailable one, standing above them, brought down upon them.
entries.23.46: 'Those brave foot-soldiers, struck through, fell away like elephants of sixty years come into a great mire.
entries.23.47: 'Seeing his sons of great might sinking and reeling, Ravana roared for joy like a great rain-cloud.
entries.23.48: 'Then that rakshasa, letting loose great roars, slew Varuna's men with weapons of many kinds, as a cloud slays with its falling torrents.
entries.23.49: 'Then all of them turned away and fell upon the ground; and they were swiftly carried from the field into their houses by their own men.
entries.23.50: 'Then the rakshasa said to them, "Let this be announced to Varuna."
entries.23.51: 'But a counsellor of Varuna named Prahasta said to Ravana: "The great king, the lord of waters, has gone indeed to the world of Brahma.
entries.23.52: '"Varuna has gone to hear the music of the gandharvas, he whom you call out to battle. What use then is this labour of yours, hero, when the king is gone? Those princes who were at hand have been beaten."
entries.23.53: 'And the lord of rakshasas, hearing that and proclaiming his own name, let loose a shout of joy and went out from Varuna's abode.
entries.23.54: 'Turning back by the very road by which he had come, that rakshasa went through the sky with his face toward Lanka.'
entries.24.1: 'As he returned in his gladness, that most evil-souled Ravana carried off upon the way the daughters of kings and sages and gods and gandharvas.
entries.24.2: 'Whatever maiden or woman that rakshasa saw who was fair to look upon, he killed her kinsmen and shut her up in his chariot.
entries.24.3: 'So too he took up into that chariot the daughters of serpents, of rakshasas, of asuras and of men, and of yakshas and danavas.
entries.24.4: 'And all of them together let fall from their grief the water born of tears, like tongues of fire — born there of sorrow and of fear.
entries.24.5: 'By those blameless ones that chariot was filled with tears of fear and grief and calamity, as the ocean is filled by rivers.
entries.24.6: 'The daughters of nagas and gandharvas, and the daughters of great sages, and the daughters of daityas and danavas, wept in that chariot by hundreds —
entries.24.7: 'long-haired, lovely of limb, their faces like the full moon, full-breasted, and shining like a diamond altar at the waist,
entries.24.8: 'lovely in the curve of their hips, women like the women of the gods, radiant as refined gold,
entries.24.9: 'trembling and reeling with grief and sorrow and fear, fair of waist. And the Pushpaka, kindled all about by the wind of their sighing,
entries.24.10: 'shone like a shut fire-chamber with the flame within it. Those women, fallen under Dashagriva's power and stricken with grief,
entries.24.11: 'were dark, with wretched faces and eyes, like does in a lion's power. And one thought there, "Will he devour me?"
entries.24.12: 'And another, sore afflicted, thought, "Or will he kill me?" And remembering their mothers and fathers, their husbands and their brothers, those women wailed together, filled with grief and sorrow.
entries.24.13: '"How will it be with my son now, without me? And how with my mother, and how with my brother, drowned in an ocean of grief?
entries.24.14: '"Alas, how shall I live without that husband of mine? Death, I beseech you, take me who am fit only for sorrow.
entries.24.15: '"What evil deed was that which I did of old in another body?"
entries.24.16: 'So all of them grieved, fallen into an ocean of sorrow: "We see now no end at all to this sorrow of ours.
entries.24.17: '"Alas, shame upon the world of men; surely there is nothing baser than this — that our husbands, being weak, were slain by the mighty Ravana
entries.24.18: '"as the stars are quenched by the sun when it rises in its season. Alas, this rakshasa is very strong, and sets himself to the means of destruction.
entries.24.19: '"Alas, holding to evil conduct, he feels no loathing of himself. In every way indeed the valour of this evil-souled one befits him,
entries.24.20: '"but this deed is unbefitting — the touching of another's wife. Since this basest of rakshasas takes his pleasure in the wives of others,
entries.24.21: '"therefore that evil-minded one shall meet his death through a woman alone." When these words had been uttered by those virtuous and noble women,
entries.24.22: 'the drums sounded in the sky and a rain of flowers fell. Cursed by those women, he was like one whose strength is struck away and whose splendour is gone;
entries.24.23: 'by those chaste and virtuous wives he was made downcast in mind. Hearing all their lamentation, that bull among rakshasas entered the city of Lanka, honoured by the night-rangers.
entries.24.24: 'At that moment a dreadful rakshasi who took what form she pleased fell suddenly upon the ground — she was Ravana's sister.
entries.24.25: 'Ravana raised his sister up and, comforting her, said, "What is this, good lady? Tell me quickly what you wish to say."
entries.24.26: 'Her eyes choked with tears and red, she said, "I have been made a widow, king, by you in your strength, and by force.
entries.24.27: '"These heroes, king, the daityas known as the Kalakeyas, fourteen thousand of them, were slain by you in battle;
entries.24.28: '"and among them was my husband, of great strength, dearer to me than life.
entries.24.29: '"He too was slain by you, dear one, as an enemy, in your greed for your brother's cause. It is by you that I am struck down, king, by my own kinsman.
entries.24.30: '"For your sake, king, I shall bear the name of widow. Surely a son-in-law should be protected by you even in battle; and he was slain by you in the fight, and you feel no shame."
entries.24.31: 'Being addressed thus by his sister as she cried out, Dashagriva comforted her and spoke these words, putting conciliation first:
entries.24.32: '"Enough of weeping, my child; you need have no fear at all. I shall take pains to content you with gifts and honours and favours.
entries.24.33: '"Reckless in battle, distracted, longing for victory and loosing my arrows, I do not know in a fight, fair one, my own men from the enemy.
entries.24.34: '"I did not know that it was my sister's husband as I struck, being mad with battle. So it was that your husband was slain by me in the fray, sister.
entries.24.35: '"But whatever can be had at this hour, that I shall do for your good. Dwell beside your brother Khara, who is endowed with lordship.
entries.24.36: '"He shall be the lord of fourteen thousand, your brother, mighty among the rakshasas, master in the march and in the giving of gifts.
entries.24.37: '"There the son of your mother's sister, this lord Khara, shall be your brother; and that night-ranger shall always do your bidding.
entries.24.38: '"Let this hero go quickly to guard the Dandaka forest. Dushana of great strength shall be the captain of his host.
entries.24.39: '"There the brave Khara shall always do your word, and he shall be the lord of rakshasas who take what shape they please."
entries.24.40: 'Having spoken thus, Dashagriva assigned him an army — fourteen thousand rakshasas endowed with valour.
entries.24.41: 'Surrounded by all those rakshasas of dreadful aspect, Khara went swiftly to the Dandaka, fearing nothing from any quarter.
entries.24.42: 'And there he made his rule, with every thorn plucked out; and Shurpanakha dwelt there in the Dandaka forest.'
entries.25.1: 'Having given that dreadful forest to Khara and comforted his sister, Dashagriva was glad and grew more at ease.
entries.25.2: 'Then that mighty lord of rakshasas entered with his followers the finest grove of Lanka, which is called Nikumbhila.
entries.25.3: 'And there he saw a sacrifice in progress, strewn with a hundred sacrificial posts and adorned with a fair sanctuary, blazing as it were with splendour.
entries.25.4: 'Then he saw there his own son, the dreadful Meghanada, wearing a black deerskin and bearing the water-pot and the sacred grass as his ensign.
entries.25.5: 'Coming to him, the lord of Lanka embraced him in his arms and said, "What is this, my son? Tell me truly."
entries.25.6: 'Then Ushanas, best of brahmins and of great austerity, said there to Ravana, best of rakshasas, that it was for the increase of his sacrificial merit:
entries.25.7: '"I shall tell you, king; let all of it be heard. Seven sacrifices of the widest scope have been performed by your son —
entries.25.8: '"the Agnishtoma, the Ashvamedha, the sacrifice rich in gold, the Rajasuya, the Gomedha and the Vaishnava too.
entries.25.9: '"And when the rite of Maheshvara was undertaken, which men can hardly attain, your son won boons here from Pashupati himself:
entries.25.10: '"a divine chariot going where it is wished, moving in the sky, and enduring; and the illusion called Tamasi, by which darkness is brought about.
entries.25.11: '"By this illusion, lord of rakshasas, once employed in battle, his course cannot be known by gods or asuras.
entries.25.12: '"And two quivers inexhaustible of arrows, and a bow hard to overcome, and a mighty weapon, king, for the destruction of enemies in battle.
entries.25.13: '"Having won all these boons, Dashanana, this son of yours — and now, at the ending of the sacrifice, I have been waiting to see you."
entries.25.14: 'Then Dashagriva said, "This is not well done, since enemies with Indra at their head have been honoured with these offerings.
entries.25.15: '"Come now, and know it for done; there is no doubt it was well done. Come, gentle one, let us go to our own house."
entries.25.16: 'Then Dashagriva went with his son and with Vibhishana, and had all those women brought down, their voices choked with tears —
entries.25.17: 'the fortunate and jewel-like women of gods and danavas and rakshasas. And that soul of dharma, knowing his mind toward them, spoke:
entries.25.18: '"With such conduct as this, which destroys fame and wealth and family, you act by your own will, knowing it to be an outrage upon your kin.
entries.25.19: '"Having outraged those kinsmen, you have brought here these fair women. And beyond you, king, Kumbhinasi has been carried off by Madhu."
entries.25.20: 'Then Ravana said, "I do not understand this. Who is this whom you name Madhu?"
entries.25.21: 'Then Vibhishana in his anger said to his brother, "Let the fruit of this sinful deed be heard, which has now come home.
entries.25.22: '"He who was the elder brother of our grandfather, the elder brother of Sumali, known as Malyavan, an aged and wise night-ranger —
entries.25.23: '"he was our mother's father's elder brother, and so our grandfather. His daughter had a daughter named Kumbhinasi,
entries.25.24: '"and that maiden, born of Anala, was the child of our mother's sister. By dharma she is a sister to us brothers.
entries.25.25: '"She was carried off, king, by the mighty rakshasa Madhu, while your son was engaged in his sacrifice and I was dwelling under the water,
entries.25.26: '"and while Kumbhakarna, great king, was in his sleep. He slew the best of the rakshasas, the counsellors honoured here,
entries.25.27: '"and outraged and carried her off as she slept in your own inner apartments. And though you heard of it, great king, you bore it, and he was not slain.
entries.25.28: '"Since a maiden must in any case be given to a husband by her brothers — this then is the fruit of that sinful deed of yours, evil-minded one.
entries.25.29: '"Let it be known to you that it has come home in this very world." Hearing Vibhishana's words, Ravana lord of rakshasas was stirred by his own wickedness like an ocean heated to boiling.
entries.25.30: 'Then Dashagriva said in anger, his eyes red: "Let my chariot be made ready at once, and let our warriors be armed.
entries.25.31: '"Let my brother Kumbhakarna and the chief among the night-rangers mount their vehicles with weapons of every kind.
entries.25.32: '"Today, having slain that Madhu in battle who has no fear of Ravana, I shall go to the world of the gods, longing for the fight and surrounded by my friends."
entries.25.33: 'Four thousand foremost divisions of the rakshasas marched out at once with weapons of many kinds, longing for battle.
entries.25.34: 'Indrajit went at the head of the host, taking the soldiers with him; Ravana went in the middle and Kumbhakarna behind.
entries.25.35: 'And the righteous Vibhishana practised dharma in Lanka; but all the rest, greatly blessed, went toward Madhu's city.
entries.25.36: 'With asses and camels and blazing horses, with porpoises and great serpents, all the rakshasas went, filling the sky without a gap.
entries.25.37: 'And daityas by hundreds who had made enmity with the gods, seeing Ravana going, followed after him.
entries.25.38: 'And Dashanana, going to Madhu's city and entering it, did not see Madhu there, but saw his sister there.
entries.25.39: 'And she, bowing with joined palms, came and laid her head at his feet —
entries.25.40: 'Kumbhinasi, terrified then of that king of rakshasas. He raised her up, saying, "You need not fear."
entries.25.41: 'And Ravana, best of rakshasas, said, "What shall I do for you?" She said, "If you are pleased with me, king, mighty-armed one, you should not slay my husband here today, giver of honour.
entries.25.42: '"For there is no fear said to be like this for women of good family; of all fears, widowhood is the greatest calamity.
entries.25.43: '"Be true to your word, lord of kings, and look upon me who ask it. And you yourself have said, great king, 'You need not fear.'"
entries.25.44: 'Then Ravana said gladly to his sister who stood there, "And where is this husband of yours? Tell me quickly.
entries.25.45: '"I shall go with him to the world of the gods to win the victory. Out of compassion and affection for you I have turned back from Madhu's death."
entries.25.46: 'Being told this, she roused that night-ranger from his sleep, and that rakshasi said to her husband as though rejoicing:
entries.25.47: '"My brother Dashagriva of great might has come, longing to conquer the world of the gods, and he chooses you for his ally.
entries.25.48: '"Go therefore with your kinsmen to help him, rakshasa. It is fitting to serve the purpose of one who is affectionate and who honours you."
entries.25.49: 'Hearing those words of hers, Madhu said, "So be it."
entries.25.50: 'And going to him in due form, he looked upon that best of rakshasas, and honoured Ravana lord of rakshasas according to dharma.
entries.25.51: 'And the valiant Dashagriva, having received that honour in Madhu's house and passed one night there, made ready to go.
entries.25.52: 'Then, coming to Kailasa, the mountain that is Vaishravana's dwelling, that lord of rakshasas, splendid as Mahendra, encamped his army.'
entries.26.1: 'And that valiant Dashagriva, when the sun had set, chose to make his camp there with his army.
entries.26.2: 'When the spotless moon had risen, matching the mountain in radiance, that great army with its many weapons lay asleep.
entries.26.3: 'But Ravana of great valour sat upon the mountain's crest, and saw its beauties lit by the moon and by the trees —
entries.26.4: 'with blazing groves of karnikara and thickets of kadamba, with lotus-pools in flower and the waters of Mandakini,
entries.26.5: 'with champaka and ashoka, punnaga and mandara trees, with mango and patala and lodhra, with priyangu and arjuna and ketaka, with tagara and coconut, with priyala and jackfruit,
entries.26.6: 'with aragvadha and tamala, with priyala and bakula too — with these and other trees the depths of the wood were lit; and there kinnaras, stricken with love and impassioned, with their sweet voices
entries.26.7: 'sang together in a way that swelled the heart's delight.
entries.26.8: 'And vidyadharas, drunk with wine and their eyes red at the corners with it, sported and made merry, mingling with their women.
entries.26.9: 'Like the ringing of bells a sweet sound was heard — the singing of the hosts of apsaras in the dwelling of the giver of wealth.
entries.26.10: 'The trees, struck by the wind, let fall showers of blossom and seemed to scent that mountain with the fragrance of the spring months.
entries.26.11: 'Bearing an abundant fragrance mingled with the pollen of honeyed flowers, a pleasant wind blew, swelling Ravana's desire.
entries.26.12: 'By the singing and the wealth of flowers, by the coolness of the wind and the virtue of the mountain, by the coming on of night and by the rising of the moon,
entries.26.13: 'Ravana of great valour fell under the sway of desire; and sighing again and again, he gazed upon the moon.
entries.26.14: 'At that moment there came by, adorned with divine ornaments, Rambha, best of all apsaras, decked with divine flowers,
entries.26.15: 'her limbs anointed with divine sandal, her hair dressed with mandara blossoms, going upon a divine festival, her face like the full moon,
entries.26.16: 'bearing her hips as a lovely offering of pleasure, full and adorned with a girdle of chains, a delight to the eye and the heart,
entries.26.17: 'with fresh marks of paint made from the flowers of the six seasons.
entries.26.18: 'She shone as though she were another among beauty and grace and radiance and modesty; and she was wrapped in a dark garment like a rain-laden cloud.
entries.26.19: 'Her face was like the moon, her brows fair as two bows, her thighs like an elephant's trunk, her hands soft as young leaves. Going through the midst of the army, she was seen by Ravana.
entries.26.20: 'And he rose and, falling under the sway of Kama's arrows, took her by the hand as she went, and said with a smile to her who was ashamed:
entries.26.21: '"Where do you go, fair one, and what fortune do you go to of your own accord? Whose hour of good fortune is this, that he shall enjoy you?
entries.26.22: '"Who today shall have his fill of the nectar of your face, fragrant as lotus and lily, like the very taste of the nectar of the gods?
entries.26.23: '"These breasts of yours, timid one, full and fair as golden jars and close together — to whose breast shall they give their touch?
entries.26.24: '"Who ascends today to those hips of yours, broad as a wheel of gold and hung with chains of gold, which are heaven itself in form?
entries.26.25: '"What man is better than I today — Shakra, or Vishnu, or the Ashvins? It is not well, timid one, that you should pass me by and go to him.
entries.26.26: '"Rest here, broad-hipped one, upon this fair slab of rock.
entries.26.27: '"There is none in the three worlds who is lord but me.
entries.26.28: '"So Dashanana asks you thus, with joined palms and bowed low. Come to me, who am the master of masters and the ordainer of the three worlds."
entries.26.29: 'Being addressed thus, Rambha said, trembling, with joined palms: "Be gracious; you should not speak so, for you are as an elder to me.
entries.26.30: '"I ought to be guarded by you from others, if I were assailed. By dharma I am your son's wife; that is the truth I tell you."
entries.26.31: 'Then Dashagriva said to her who stood with her face bent to his feet, and whose hair stood on end at the mere sight of him:
entries.26.32: '"If you are my son's wife, then you would be my daughter-in-law." And Rambha said in answer to Ravana, "Even so.
entries.26.33: '"By dharma I am your son's wife, bull among rakshasas — the son dearer than life to your brother Vaishravana, renowned in the three worlds as Nalakubara.
entries.26.34: '"He who by dharma might be a brahmin and by valour a kshatriya, who in anger might be fire itself and in forbearance the equal of the earth —
entries.26.35: '"to him, the son of a guardian of the world, I am pledged. It is for his sake that all this adorning has been done.
entries.26.36: '"So my heart is set upon him and upon no other.
entries.26.37: '"By that truth, king, you ought to release me, subduer of foes.
entries.26.38: '"For that soul of dharma stands waiting for me in eagerness. You should not put a hindrance in your son's way here; release me.
entries.26.39: '"Go by the road that good men walk, bull among rakshasas. You are to be honoured by me, and I am to be protected by you."
entries.26.40: 'Being addressed thus, Dashagriva answered in a manner that seemed courteous: "As for your saying that you are my daughter-in-law — this holds among women who have one husband. This is the way of the world of the gods, and held eternal among the gods:
entries.26.41: '"the apsaras have no husband, nor is any one of them taken as a wife."
entries.26.42: 'And having said this, that rakshasa set her down upon the rock and, wholly given to the enjoyment of desire, took her by force.
entries.26.43: 'Then Rambha, being released, her garland and ornaments torn away, was like a river churned by the sporting of a lordly elephant,
entries.26.44: 'her hair disordered and loose, her hands trembling like young leaves, as a flowering creeper is shaken by the wind.
entries.26.45: 'Trembling and ashamed and afraid, with joined palms she came to Nalakubara and fell at his feet.
entries.26.46: 'Seeing her in that state, the great-souled Nalakubara said, "What is this, good lady, that you have fallen at my feet?"
entries.26.47: 'And she, sighing and trembling, with joined palms, began to tell him all as it truly was:
entries.26.48: '"This Dashagriva, lord, has come here on his way to the third heaven, and with his army for companion he has passed this night here.
entries.26.49: '"He saw me as I came toward you, subduer of foes; and that rakshasa seized me and asked me, 'Whose are you?'
entries.26.50: '"And I told him all that was true. But his soul was overcome by the confusion of desire, and he did not hear that word of mine.
entries.26.51: '"Though I begged him, lord, saying, 'I am your daughter-in-law' — he put all of it behind him and outraged me by force.
entries.26.52: '"So you should forgive this fault of mine, holder of good vows. For the strength of a woman and of a man is not equal, gentle one."
entries.26.53: 'Hearing this, the son of Vaishravana was seized with wrath; and hearing of that great outrage he entered into meditation.
entries.26.54: 'And knowing then that deed of his, the son of Vaishravana, his eyes red with anger within a moment, took water in his hand.
entries.26.55: 'Taking that water and sipping it in due form, he loosed a dreadful curse upon the lord of rakshasas:
entries.26.56: '"Since you were outraged by him by force and against your will, good lady, therefore he shall not go to any other young woman against her will.
entries.26.57: '"And when, stricken with desire, he shall force a woman who is unwilling, then his head shall be split into seven pieces."
entries.26.58: 'When that curse had been uttered, bright as blazing fire, the drums of the gods sounded and a rain of flowers fell from the sky; and all the gods with the Grandsire at their head rejoiced.
entries.26.59: 'Knowing the whole course of the world and the death of that rakshasa, the sages and the fathers were filled with the highest joy.
entries.26.60: 'And Dashagriva, hearing of that curse which made the hair stand on end, no longer set his mind upon union with women who were unwilling.
entries.26.61: 'And all the women he had carried away, being chaste, took joy in it, hearing the curse loosed by Nalakubara, which was dear to their hearts.'
entries.27.1: 'Then, having passed over Kailasa, that night-ranger Dashagriva of great splendour came to the world of Indra.
entries.27.2: 'And as that army of rakshasas drew near from every side, a sound went up to the world of the gods like the churning of the ocean.
entries.27.3: 'Hearing that Ravana had come, Indra rose from his seat and said to all the gods gathered there —
entries.27.4: 'to the Adityas and the Vasus, the Rudras and the Vishvedevas, the Sadhyas and the hosts of Maruts: "Make ready for battle against the evil-souled Ravana."
entries.27.5: 'Being addressed thus by Shakra, those gods, the equals of Shakra in the fight, of great courage, armed themselves and were filled with a will to battle.
entries.27.6: 'But Mahendra, wretched and terrified because of Ravana, came into Vishnu's presence and spoke these words:
entries.27.7: '"Vishnu, what shall I do? That mighty rakshasa, whose valour and prowess are great, comes on for battle.
entries.27.8: '"He is strong through the granting of a boon and by no other cause; and that true word which the lotus-born spoke must be made good.
entries.27.9: '"As Namuchi and Vritra, Bali and Naraka and Shambara were burnt up by me when I leaned upon your strength — so do now.
entries.27.10: '"For there is no other, lord of the gods of gods, slayer of Madhu, but you. In the three worlds with all that moves and does not move there is no refuge and no resort.
entries.27.11: '"You are the glorious Narayana, the lotus-navelled, the eternal. By you were these worlds established, and Shakra, and I, lord of the gods.
entries.27.12: '"By you was all this threefold world created with what moves and does not move; and into you, lord, all things enter at the ending of an age.
entries.27.13: '"Tell me therefore truly, god of gods, yourself: will you with your discus for helper fight against Ravana, lord?"
entries.27.14: 'Being addressed thus by Shakra, the lord god Narayana said, "No terror need be felt; hear me.
entries.27.15: '"This evil-souled one cannot yet be conquered by gods or asuras, nor slain when he is met, unconquerable as he is through the gift of a boon.
entries.27.16: '"In every way that rakshasa, swollen with strength, will do a great deed together with his son; this has been seen from the nature of things.
entries.27.17: '"As for what you said to me, lord of the gods — 'Fight' — I shall not fight against that rakshasa Ravana in battle.
entries.27.18: '"Vishnu does not turn back from a fight without slaying his enemy; and that desire is hard to attain today against a Ravana guarded by his boon.
entries.27.19: '"But I promise you, lord of the gods, Shatakratu, in your presence: I shall be the cause of that rakshasa's death.
entries.27.20: '"I myself shall be his slayer, Ravana with all who go before him; and I shall gladden the gods, knowing that the time has come. This is the truth I have told you, king of the gods, lord of Shachi.
entries.27.21: '"Fight without fear, mighty one, together with them all."
entries.27.22: 'Then the Rudras with the Adityas, the Vasus, the Maruts and the Ashvins, armed, marched swiftly out of the city against the rakshasas on every side.
entries.27.23: 'At that moment, at the ending of night, a roar was heard from every side of that army of Ravana as it joined battle.
entries.27.24: 'Those of great valour, engaging and looking upon one another, turned gladly toward the fight.
entries.27.25: 'Then a great commotion arose among the armies of the gods, seeing that undiminished host at the head of the battle.
entries.27.26: 'Then there was a battle between gods and danavas and rakshasas, dreadful and full of tumult, with weapons of many kinds upraised.
entries.27.27: 'At that moment those brave rakshasas of dreadful aspect, the ministers of Ravana, came forward for the fight —
entries.27.28: 'Maricha and Prahasta, Mahaparshva and Mahodara, Akampana and Nikumbha, Shuka and Sarana,
entries.27.29: 'Samhlada and Dhumaketu, Mahadamshtra and Ghatodara, Jambumali and Mahahrada, and the rakshasa Virupaksha,
entries.27.30: 'Suptaghna and Yajnakopa, Durmukha, Dushana and Khara, Trishiras and Karaviraksha, and the rakshasa Suryashatru,
entries.27.31: 'Mahakaya and Atikaya, Devantaka and Narantaka — surrounded by all these, that one of great valour and great strength,
entries.27.32: 'Sumali, Ravana's grandfather, plunged into the host. In great wrath he shattered all the ranks of the gods with sharp weapons of many kinds, as the wind shatters the clouds.
entries.27.33: 'That force of the gods, Rama, struck down by the night-rangers, was driven from every quarter like deer driven by a lion.
entries.27.34: 'At that moment the brave Vasu, eighth of the Vasus, known as Savitra, entered the field of battle.
entries.27.35: 'And so too the two Adityas of great valour, Tvashtri and Pushan, armed and fearless, entered the fight with their forces.
entries.27.36: 'Then there was a battle of the gods with the rakshasas — with the glory of those wrathful rakshasas who never turn from a fight.
entries.27.37: 'Then all those rakshasas struck down the gods who stood in that battle with dreadful weapons of many kinds, by hundreds of thousands.
entries.27.38: 'And the gods with their bright weapons sent to the abode of Yama those dreadful rakshasas of great strength and valour.
entries.27.39: 'At that moment, Rama, a rakshasa named Sumali came in wrath upon that host with weapons of many kinds.
entries.27.40: 'And in his fury he shattered the whole force of the gods with sharp weapons of many kinds, as the wind shatters a cloud.
entries.27.41: 'Struck by his showers of great arrows and by his dreadful pikes and darts, all the gods could not keep their ranks together.
entries.27.42: 'Then, as the gods were being driven back by Sumali, the eighth of the Vasus, Savitra, stood forth in wrath.
entries.27.43: 'Surrounded by his own ranks of chariots, that one of great splendour held back by his valour that night-ranger who was striking them down.
entries.27.44: 'Then there was a great battle between those two that made the hair stand on end —
entries.27.45: 'between Sumali and the Vasu, neither turning from the field. Then by the great arrows of that great-souled Vasu his serpent-drawn chariot was destroyed and struck down in a moment.
entries.27.46: 'Having destroyed his chariot in the fight, thick with a hundred arrows, the Vasu took up his mace in his hand to slay him.
entries.27.47: 'Then, taking up that mace with its blazing point, like the staff of Time, Savitra brought it down upon Sumali's head.
entries.27.48: 'Falling upon him, that mace shone like a meteor, roaring like Indra's great thunderbolt upon a mountain.
entries.27.49: 'Neither bone nor head nor flesh of his could then be seen; by that mace he was reduced to ashes as he was slain upon the field.
entries.27.50: 'Seeing him slain in the battle, the rakshasas on every side fled away together, crying out to one another; and driven back by the Vasu, the rakshasas would not stand.'
entries.28.1: 'Seeing Sumali slain and reduced to ashes by the Vasu, and marking his own army broken and tormented by the gods,
entries.28.2: 'the mighty son of Ravana in his wrath turned all the rakshasas back and took his stand — Meghanada.
entries.28.3: 'That great warrior, in his fine chariot the colour of fire that goes where it is wished, rushed upon that army like fire blazing among the woods.
entries.28.4: 'And as he entered, bearing weapons of many kinds, the gods fled to every quarter at the mere sight of him.
entries.28.5: 'There was none then who would face him as he sought the fight; and seeing them all struck through and terrified, Shakra said to the gods:
entries.28.6: '"Do not fear and do not flee; turn back to the battle, gods. My son goes there, the unconquered, for the fight."
entries.28.7: 'Then the god who was Shakra's son, renowned as Jayanta, came into the battle in a chariot of wondrous make.
entries.28.8: 'Then all the gods surrounded the son of Shachi and, coming upon Ravana's son in the fight, struck at him.
entries.28.9: 'And there was a fight between them worthy of gods and rakshasas — between Mahendra's son and the son of the lord of rakshasas.
entries.28.10: 'Then the son of the rakshasa brought down upon Gomukha, the charioteer and son of Matali, arrows adorned with gold.
entries.28.11: 'And Jayanta, son of Shachi, did the same to his charioteer; and Ravana's son in his wrath pierced him too from every side.
entries.28.12: 'For that mighty one, filled with anger and his eyes wide, covered the son of Shakra with showers of arrows.
entries.28.13: 'Then in great wrath he brought down upon the armies of the gods weapons of many kinds with keen edges, by thousands —
entries.28.14: 'shataghnis and pestles, darts and maces, swords and battle-axes, and great peaks of mountains Ravana's son brought down.
entries.28.15: 'Then the worlds were shaken and darkness came, as that son of Ravana struck down the armies of his enemies.
entries.28.16: 'Then that force of the gods on every side, and the son of Shachi with them, was made distressed in many ways, tormented by his arrows.
entries.28.17: 'They could not tell one another apart, whether rakshasa or god; here and there all was overturned and ran about in confusion.
entries.28.18: 'Gods struck down gods, and rakshasas rakshasas; bewildered and covered by that darkness, others fled away.
entries.28.19: 'At that moment a brave and valiant lord of the daityas named Puloma seized the son of Shachi and carried him away.
entries.28.20: 'Seizing his daughter's son, he entered the ocean; for he was Jayanta's grandfather, that Puloma of whom Shachi was the daughter.
entries.28.21: 'Knowing then that Jayanta was gone, all the gods were joyless and, being troubled, fled away.
entries.28.22: 'And Ravana's son in his wrath, surrounded by his own forces, rushed upon those gods and let loose a great roar.
entries.28.23: 'Seeing his son gone and the gods put to flight, the lord of the gods said to Matali, "Let my chariot be brought."
entries.28.24: 'And that divine and dreadful great chariot, made ready, was brought up by Matali, driven at great speed.
entries.28.25: 'Then before that chariot great clouds charged with lightning, swift as the wind, thundered with a mighty noise.
entries.28.26: 'Instruments of many kinds were sounded and the gandharvas sang with one mind, and the hosts of apsaras danced, as the lord of the thirty went forth.
entries.28.27: 'Surrounded by Rudras and Vasus and Adityas, by Sadhyas and the hosts of Maruts, bearing weapons of many kinds, the lord of the thirty went out.
entries.28.28: 'But as Shakra went forth a harsh wind blew, the sun lost its brightness, and great meteors fell.
entries.28.29: 'At that moment the brave and mighty Dashagriva mounted a divine chariot made by Vishvakarma,
entries.28.30: 'wound about with great and dreadful serpents that made the hair stand on end, so that it seemed ablaze in the battle with the breath of them.
entries.28.31: 'Surrounded by daityas and night-rangers, that chariot went forward; and turning toward the fight, he came against Mahendra.
entries.28.32: 'But he held his son back and took his stand himself; and Ravana's son withdrew from the fight and sat down.
entries.28.33: 'Then the battle of the gods with the rakshasas went on, dreadful as clouds pouring down their weapons in the fray.
entries.28.34: 'And Kumbhakarna, evil-souled, with weapons of many kinds upraised, did not know in that fight with whom he was fighting.
entries.28.35: 'With his teeth and his arms and his feet, with spears and javelins and arrows, with whatever came to hand he struck at the gods in his fury.
entries.28.36: 'Then that night-ranger, meeting with the most terrible of the Rudras and fighting them in the battle, was wounded without pause by their weapons.
entries.28.37: 'His body thick with weapons and streaming blood, Kumbhakarna shone like a rain-laden cloud with the roar of thunder and lightning.
entries.28.38: 'Then that army of the rakshasas, fighting with the hosts of Maruts, was wholly driven from the field by sharp weapons of many kinds.
entries.28.39: 'Some, slain and cut down, writhed upon the earth; and others still clung to their mounts and stood in the fight.
entries.28.40: 'Chariots and elephants, asses and camels, serpents and horses in the battle, porpoises and boars and creatures with the faces of pishachas —
entries.28.41: 'clinging to these with their arms, some stood propped upright; and the night-rangers, pierced by the weapons of the gods, died.
entries.28.42: 'That confusion of battle looked like a painted scene, with the rakshasas slain and stupefied upon the earth.
entries.28.43: 'A river ran at the front of the fight, its waters blood, thronged with kanka birds and vultures, and bearing weapons as its crocodiles.
entries.28.44: 'At that moment the mighty Dashagriva in wrath, seeing his whole force struck down by the gods,
entries.28.45: 'plunged swiftly into that swelling ocean of armies against them, and slaying the gods in the battle came straight against Shakra.
entries.28.46: 'Shakra came on, drawing his great bow with a mighty sound, at the twanging of which the ten quarters resounded.
entries.28.47: 'Drawing that great bow, Indra brought down upon Ravana's head arrows bright as fire and the sun.
entries.28.48: 'And in the same way the mighty-armed Dashagriva stood firm and covered Shakra with showers of arrows loosed from his bow.
entries.28.49: 'And as those two fought with showers of arrows on every side, nothing could then be known, for all was wrapped in darkness.'
entries.29.1: 'Then, when the darkness had come, all those gods and rakshasas fought on, wild with strength, destroying one another.
entries.29.2: 'And by the army of the gods a tenth part of the great force of the rakshasas was left standing in the battle, and the rest was sent to Yama's abode.
entries.29.3: 'In that battle of darkness all those gods and rakshasas fighting could not tell one another apart.
entries.29.4: 'But Indra and Ravana and the mighty son of Ravana — those three were not bewildered in that net of darkness.
entries.29.5: 'And Ravana, seeing his whole force struck down in a moment, was seized with a fierce anger and let loose a great roar.
entries.29.6: 'And that unassailable one said in his wrath to his charioteer who stood in the chariot, "Carry me to the very end, through the midst of the enemy's host.
entries.29.7: '"Today I shall myself send all these gods by my valour to Yama's abode with dreadful weapons of many kinds.
entries.29.8: '"I shall slay Indra, and the giver of wealth, and Varuna, and Yama; and having slain the gods I shall stand above them all. There is no need to despair; drive my chariot swiftly.
entries.29.9: '"Twice now I say to you, carry me to the very end.
entries.29.10: '"This is the region of the Nandana grove where we now are. Carry me today to where the mountain of sunrise is."
entries.29.11: 'Hearing his words, the charioteer urged those horses swift as thought straight through the midst of the enemy.
entries.29.12: 'And knowing his resolve, Shakra lord of the gods, standing in his chariot upon the field, spoke to the gods:
entries.29.13: '"Gods, hear my word, what seems best to me. Let this rakshasa Dashagriva be well taken alive.
entries.29.14: '"For this one of great strength will go on with his armies and his chariot swift as the wind, like the ocean with its swelling waves at the full moon.
entries.29.15: '"He cannot be slain today, being fearless through the gift of a boon. Let us therefore take that rakshasa; be ready in the fight.
entries.29.16: '"As the three worlds are enjoyed by me since Bali was bound, so the binding of this sinful one seems good to me."
entries.29.17: 'Then Shakra, taking another station and leaving Ravana, fought on, great king, terrifying the rakshasas in the battle.
entries.29.18: 'Dashagriva entered from the north without turning back, and Shatakratu entered by the southern flank.
entries.29.19: 'Then that lord of rakshasas, having entered a hundred yojanas, covered the whole force of the gods with showers of arrows.
entries.29.20: 'Then Shakra, seeing his own force destroyed, unshaken, turned back and encircled Dashanana.
entries.29.21: 'At that moment a cry went up from the danavas and rakshasas — "Alas, we are slain!" — seeing Ravana caught by Shakra.
entries.29.22: 'Then Ravana's son, mounting his chariot in a swoon of anger, entered that dreadful host in great fury.
entries.29.23: 'Entering into that great illusion obtained of old from the lord of cattle, he plunged in wrath and rushed upon that army.
entries.29.24: 'Leaving all the gods, he rushed straight upon Shakra; and Mahendra of great splendour could not see his enemy's son.
entries.29.25: 'Though his armour was cast off and he was being struck there by the gods of great valour, Ravana's son took no notice at all.
entries.29.26: 'Striking Matali as he came on with the finest of his arrows, he covered Mahendra again with a rain of shafts.
entries.29.27: 'Then Shakra left his chariot and dismissed his charioteer, and mounting Airavata he sought out Ravana's son.
entries.29.28: 'But he, strong in illusion, unseen and moving in the sky, wrapped Indra about in his illusion and rushed at him with his arrows.
entries.29.29: 'And when Ravana's son knew Indra to be worn out, he bound him then by his illusion and carried him off to his own army.
entries.29.30: 'Seeing Mahendra taken by force from that great battle, all the immortals wondered, "What can this be?"
entries.29.31: '"That master of illusion is not to be seen, the conqueror of Shakra, victorious in the fray, by whom Indra, for all his knowledge, is carried off by force through illusion."
entries.29.32: 'At that moment all the hosts of the gods in wrath turned Ravana back and covered him with showers of arrows.
entries.29.33: 'And Ravana, meeting the Adityas and the Vasus then, was tormented by his enemies and could not fight in that battle.
entries.29.34: 'Seeing him spent and his body broken by blows, Ravana's son, showing himself, said to his father in the fight:
entries.29.35: '"Come, father, let us go; let this work of war be ended. Know that we have conquered; be at ease and free of fever.
entries.29.36: '"For this one who is lord of the army of the gods and of the three worlds has been taken by the power of fate, and the pride of the gods is broken.
entries.29.37: '"Enjoy the three worlds as you wish, having subdued your enemy by your might. What use is this labour of yours? The fight today is fruitless."
entries.29.38: 'Then the hosts of the gods turned back from the work of war; and hearing Ravana's son speak so, he became easy in mind.
entries.29.39: 'Then that lord, free of the fever of battle and having won the victory, went gladly toward his own dwelling, that lord of night-rangers; and coming to his son, he said:
entries.29.40: '"By those deeds of valour of yours, worthy of great strength, the honour of my house has been increased — in that today this lord of the thirty of unmatched might, and the thirty with him, have been conquered by you.
entries.29.41: '"Set Vasava upon your chariot and take him; go from here to the city surrounded by your army. I too shall follow swiftly behind you with my counsellors as you go."
entries.29.42: 'Then that valiant son of Ravana, surrounded by his force and his mounts, took the lord of the thirty and, coming to his own dwelling, dismissed the rakshasas who had fought.'
entries.30.1: 'When the mighty Mahendra had been conquered by Ravana's son, the gods then went to Lanka, putting Prajapati at their head.
entries.30.2: 'And coming there to Ravana, surrounded by his sons and brothers, Prajapati, standing in the sky, said with conciliation first:
entries.30.3: '"Child Ravana, I am pleased with your son in the battle. Ah, his valour and nobility are equal to yours, or greater.
entries.30.4: '"For the whole three worlds have been conquered by you through your own splendour; your vow has been made fruitful, and I am pleased with your son.
entries.30.5: '"And this son of yours, Ravana, of great strength and valour, shall be renowned in the world by the name Indrajit.
entries.30.6: '"That rakshasa shall be mighty and hard to conquer, upon whom you leaned, king, and set the thirty beneath your sway.
entries.30.7: '"Let therefore Mahendra, the chastiser of Paka, be released, mighty-armed one. And let the dwellers in heaven give something for his release."
entries.30.8: 'Then Indrajit of great splendour, victorious in the fray, said, "I choose deathlessness, god, if he is to be released."
entries.30.9: 'And Prajapati said, "There is no complete deathlessness for any living creature on earth, among four-footed things or birds, or among beings of great might,
entries.30.10: '"for trees, shrubs, bushes, creepers, grasses, stones or mountains.
entries.30.11: '"All creatures fear one another when there is cause to fear; and so in this world there would be fear of every man for everything."
entries.30.12: 'Hearing what the Grandsire, the imperishable lord, had said, Indrajit
entries.30.13: 'of great strength then said to him who stood there: "Let it be heard, then, how the freeing of Shatakratu may be accomplished.
entries.30.14: '"When I have worshipped the fire always with oblations and with mantras, and am about to go down into battle desiring victory over my foes,
entries.30.15: '"let a chariot yoked with horses rise for me out of the fire. Standing in it, let there be deathlessness for me: this is my chosen boon.
entries.30.16: '"But if I go to fight in battle, god, when that muttering and oblation to the fire is not complete, then let my destruction come.
entries.30.17: '"For every man, god, wins deathlessness by penance; but I have brought this deathlessness about by my valour."
entries.30.18: 'And the god and Grandsire said to him, "So be it." Then Shakra was released by Indrajit, and the gods went to the third heaven.
entries.30.19: 'At that time, Rama, Indra, wretched and his splendour fallen from him, his soul filled with brooding, gave himself to meditation.
entries.30.20: 'Seeing him in that state, the god Prajapati said, "Shatakratu, what great sin did you do of old?
entries.30.21: '"Lord of the immortals, many creatures were created by me, all of one colour, of one speech, and one in form.
entries.30.22: '"There was no difference among them in appearance or in mark. Then with a single mind I pondered upon those creatures,
entries.30.23: '"and to make a difference among them I fashioned one woman. Whatever was best in each limb of my creatures, that was taken out.
entries.30.24: '"So by me was the woman Ahalya fashioned in beauty and in virtue. Halya is the word here for what is ugly, and hence what comes of it;
entries.30.25: '"and since in her there was no halya, she was renowned as A-halya. So, Shakra, the name Ahalya was given her by me.
entries.30.26: '"And when that woman was made, lord of the gods, bull among the gods, my thought was, whose shall she be?
entries.30.27: '"But you, Shakra, knew that woman then in your mind, thinking, 'By right of my station she is my wife,' Purandara.
entries.30.28: '"But she was left by me as a trust with the great-souled Gautama; and having been left with him for many years, she was returned by him.
